title_en: Here's everything GTA+ gets you in GTA 6: Is it worth $8 a month?
title_fa: Here's everything GTA+ gets you in GTA 6: Is it worth $8 a month?
excerpt_en: A GTA+ membership adds a few extras to GTA 6 for $8 a month. Here's what's included and which players are most likely to get their money's worth.
excerpt_fa: A GTA+ membership adds a few extras to GTA 6 for $8 a month. Here's what's included and which players are most likely to get their money's worth.
content_en:
Here's everything GTA+ gets you in GTA 6: Is it worth $8 a month?
GTA+ adds a few perks to GTA 6 and one of them is already stirring up players.
A lot has changed in gaming in the 13 years since Grand Theft Auto 5 debuted. That includes the explosion of live-service games and gaming subscriptions, and the Grand Theft Auto franchise has gotten in on both with GTA Online and the GTA+ membership. Now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, GTA+ members get some additional benefits in the new game on top of what the subscription already offers in GTA Online.
If you're new to GTA+, you can sign up for it in-game or through your console's digital storefront. Digital pre-orders of GTA 6 on PlayStation and Xbox also included a free month of GTA+ to try it out. If you didn't pre-order or you want to keep the subscription after the free month ends, it costs $8 a month.
What GTA+ adds to the game
That $8 gets you a few perks in GTA 6, but nothing game-changing. You'll get 10 percent more money for any eligible vehicles you sell in the game and a 10 percent discount at a variety of stores. You can also use in-game transport options like scooters, bikes and public transit for free and get a premium membership to the RydeMe rideshare service. Together, those perks add up to a few cheaper ways to get around GTA 6's huge map and an easier time making cash. That can make a big difference in your progress early in the game, since cheats don't unlock until you beat the story.
The biggest and most controversial benefit is one you can claim only after reaching GTA 6's third chapter. At that point, you'll get the '90 Annis Venturas BLVD Elegy, a free sports car, plus a garage in the Crosstown area. Locking exclusive items in a single-player game behind a monthly subscription is never popular, and players have already voiced their displeasure on Reddit.
GTA+ makes more sense for GTA Online players
For most players, the GTA+ subscription fee probably isn't worth it for what it adds to GTA 6 alone. From the start, GTA+ has focused mostly on GTA Online, giving members in-game currency and discounts, new vehicles and garages to store them in, and a rotating suite of items and features. For dedicated GTA Online players who also picked up GTA 6, there's a much better case for the subscription.
The game library included with GTA+ might make it worth it for more people. Anyone with an active subscription also gets access to a selection of Rockstar's other games, including Red Dead Redemption and GTA 5. Of course, you might not have time for any of those until you finish a campaign that can run 80 hours, but the library does make the $8 subscription much easier to justify.

title_en: Multiplying your Switch 2’s storage costs less than usual right now
title_fa: Multiplying your Switch 2’s storage costs less than usual right now
excerpt_en: Expanding your Nintendo Switch 2’s 256GB of built-in storage with a microSD card is pricier than it was with Nintendo’s original console. That’s because microSD Express cards, while physically identical to ones you might have lying around, have faster read and write speeds....
excerpt_fa: Expanding your Nintendo Switch 2’s 256GB of built-in storage with a microSD card is pricier than it was with Nintendo’s original console. That’s because microSD Express cards, while physically identical to ones you might have lying around, have faster read and write speeds....
content_en:
Expanding your Nintendo Switch 2’s 256GB of built-in storage with a microSD card is pricier than it was with Nintendo’s original console. That’s because microSD Express cards, while physically identical to ones you might have lying around, have faster read and write speeds. Thankfully, Samsung’s 256GB model has dropped to $44.99 at Amazon ahead of Black Friday, which is a few bucks off its usual price but still well below its $79.99 MSRP. Sandisk’s 256GB card, meanwhile, is available for $49.99 ($10 off Amazon’s typical list price) from Amazon and Sandisk, if you prefer one brand over the other for some reason.
Multiplying your Switch 2’s storage costs less than usual right now
SSD costs are still sky-high, but at least there are decent deals on microSD Express cards.
SSD costs are still sky-high, but at least there are decent deals on microSD Express cards.
For those who don’t want to think about upgrading their Switch 2’s storage again, both brands’ 512GB microSD Express cards are selling for a fair $99.99 on Amazon. That gives you double the storage for roughly twice the price of a 256GB card, as it should be.
I suspect the 256GB option will be enough for most Switch 2 players, unless you buy a lot of games. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is 24.9 gigabytes, for example. Other Nintendo-developed games tend to be similar in install size, though it’s all over the place for third-party game makers; Resident Evil Requiem (which also recently dropped to $39.99 on Amazon) is relatively small at 28.7 gigs, while The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is about 50. Some games take up even more storage.

excerpt_fa: Google is announcing some significant changes to its smart home software. Starting next year, the company will shut down the Nest app in favor of the Google Home app and retire Google Assistant on its smart home devices. The Nest app shutdown takes place on January 25th, 2027,...
content_en:
Google is announcing some significant changes to its smart home software. Starting next year, the company will shut down the Nest app in favor of the Google Home app and retire Google Assistant on its smart home devices.
Google says it’s going to shut off Google Assistant on smart speakers next year
Google is making some big changes to its smart home offerings, including killing the Nest app.
Google is making some big changes to its smart home offerings, including killing the Nest app.
The Nest app shutdown takes place on January 25th, 2027, meaning you’ll have to manage your Nest products, including Nest thermostats, cameras, and Nest Protect alarms, from the Google Home app instead. If you get the Google Home app set up, Google will move over your Nest devices, including cameras and video history, to the Home app on that January 25th date. The company will also automatically transfer Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions to Google Home Premium. Google says it will begin deleting Nest account data on March 25th, 2027.
The changes for Google Assistant will take place later: On August 2nd, 2027, the Gemini for Home voice assistant will replace Google Assistant on smart speakers and smart displays, the company says. Google argues that Gemini for Home allows users to ask more complex questions and speak naturally instead of needing to use dedicated commands or specific language.

title_en: OpenAI brings its collaborative Space hubs to Plus users
title_fa: OpenAI brings its collaborative Space hubs to Plus users
excerpt_en: You can upload documents, files and more to the hubs for easy sharing.
excerpt_fa: You can upload documents, files and more to the hubs for easy sharing.
content_en:
OpenAI brings its collaborative Space hubs to Plus users
You can upload documents, files and more to the hubs for easy sharing.
Back at its Dev Day event in September, OpenAI debuted ChatGPT Space. It's a hub that allows you, your coworkers or friends and any Dot agents you've set up to share information and collaborate on documents and other files. On release, ChatGPT Space was available to users on the company's Pro, Business and Enterprise plans. Now, OpenAI is expanding availability to those paying for its $20 per month Plus subscription. If you're one those people, you can create your own Spaces starting today.
You can create your first one by selecting "Space" from the left-hand navigation bar. It's where the Library section used to live. From there, click or tap the plus icon to make your first Space, and select a template or start uploading pages, slides, spreadsheets, images or links to websites. "Pages are a great place to start: they're a new type of document built specifically for the work you do with agents, like writing, visualizing, researching and coding," OpenAI explains. "Pages can stay automatically updated from your connected tools, too."
Spaces work with ChatGPT's recently revamped Scheduled Tasks feature, and you can invite others to collaborate on your projects with you. As a Plus user, you can't use a Dot with your Spaces (or at all, for that matter), but that's likely to change soon, with OpenAI starting to test the agents with a select group of Plus subscribers as of yesterday. As for use cases, the company suggests you can use a Space to create a city guide for a friend that plans to visit your home soon. As you find new spots, you can add them to the guide for ChatGPT to organize. For students, you can use the feature to create a study guide with 3D visuals and questions to quiz yourself. As with most of these kind of tools, a little bit of creativity goes a long way.

title_en: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?
title_fa: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?
excerpt_en: Lenders don't want SpaceX shooting their collateral into orbit. What does that mean for space data centers writ large?
excerpt_fa: Lenders don't want SpaceX shooting their collateral into orbit. What does that mean for space data centers writ large?
content_en:
The push to build data centers in space faces plenty of obstacles, from tricky engineering to a dearth of rockets that could take chips to orbit. But what about paying for the chips?
The data center ecosystem currently depends on debt financing, with cloud providers borrowing to build out data centers and then paying back the loans with a share of the revenue.
Those deals typically use the chips as collateral — if the data centers default on their loans, the lenders can take possession of the chips and resell them. That backstop makes it cheaper for companies to finance their chips. Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research, some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024.
But you’re not going to repossess chips installed in a satellite orbiting 300 miles above Earth at 17,500 miles per hour. The Financial Times is reporting that lenders behind SpaceX’s $40 billion chip financing deal asked that none of the chips purchased be used for the company’s orbital data center plans. It’s not clear if they succeeded in getting SpaceX to agree with the provision.
That may not matter to the company in the near term — SpaceX’s ability to deploy compute at terrestrial ground stations has proven lucrative, and on the company’s most recent earnings call, CEO Elon Musk detailed how he was dispatching engineers from the company’s rocket team to accelerate that build-out by taking on challenges like casting turbine blades for generators at faster than existing suppliers.
However, open questions remain about how easy it will be to find land and power to support the data center build-out. Many potential projects face delays and local opposition, while markets wait to see the state of compute demand and the ability of its buyers to turn it into revenue.
Musk, meanwhile, began saying at the beginning of 2026 that he believes space will be the “cheapest” place to operate data centers in two to three years. That’s unlikely until SpaceX can fly its Starship rocket in a fully reusable configuration. In its most recent flight test, the company failed to recover the booster stage but did succeed in landing the orbital stage of the rocket back at its launch facility in Texas. It’s not clear, though, when the second stage will fly again or how expensive it will be to prepare it for a second trip to space.
Even with Starship, however, SpaceX — as well as startups like StarCloud, Cowboy Space Corporation, Sophia Space, Orbital, and others — will need to buy chips. If the already daunting economics of space data centers weren’t challenging enough, it looks like they’ll be spending more to buy them than their terrestrial counterparts.
That might be an advantage for Google, which is focused on deploying its own TPU chips in space through Project Suncatcher. SpaceX and Tesla are working together to build their own chip foundry, Terafab, in the U.S., but that project has yet to break ground and will require years and billions of dollars before it starts producing semiconductors at scale.

A new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch can make a great holiday gift, but they can also take a pretty big dent out of your budget. That’s especially true this year, as rising hardware prices have made MacBooks and other Apple devices even more expensive. Fortunately, Black Friday offers a chance to save, especially since great deals are already available on a wide range of Apple devices. Some discounts even extend to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro, which have dropped to new lows.
Here are the Apple deals actually worth picking up ahead of Black Friday
From AirPods to Apple Watches, many Apple devices are already seeing notable discounts ahead of November 27th.
From AirPods to Apple Watches, many Apple devices are already seeing notable discounts ahead of November 27th.
Most of the discounts below are promoted as Black Friday deals, but we’ve also included a few that aren’t technically part of the shopping event but have “coincidentally” dropped in price in the last week or so. Black Friday isn’t until November 27th, however, so some prices could fall further in the coming days. Apple is also kicking off its own Black Friday shopping event that day, offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases. That said, if you don’t want to wait, we think the deals below are already worth taking advantage of.
Featured Products
Earbud and headphone deals
AirPods Pro 3
The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review.
Beats Powerbeats Pro 2
Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review.
- You can buy the AirPods 4 on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. Apple’s last-gen earbuds lack active noise cancellation, but they still deliver good, relatively bass-rich sound, even if they don’t quite match the newer AirPods 5. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review.
- The second-gen AirPods Max are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon, which is $19 shy of their best price to date (Best Buy and Target also have them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review.
Beats Studio Pro
The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review.
Beats 360 headphones
The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.
- If you want over-ears and are comfortable going without active noise cancellation, the Beats Solo 4 are down to $79.99 ($120 off) at Target in pink and white through November 22nd, marking a new low price. Amazon also has the pink headphones on sale for $79.99, while other colors are $20 more at both retailers. The headphones are a noticeable improvement over their predecessor, delivering more detailed sound and support for lossless audio. They also last up to 50 hours on a single charge, while their memory foam ear cushions make them comfortable enough for long listening sessions. Read our review.
- The Beats Studio Buds Plus are down to around $89.95 ($80 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, nearly matching their lowest price to date. The wireless earbuds feature a slick, eye-catching transparent option and solid noise cancellation, especially at this price. They’re also exceptionally comfortable, with four ear tip sizes to help you find a secure fit. Sure, you don’t get wireless charging, but they offer IPX4 water resistance and up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge. Read our review.
MacBook deals
MacBook Neo
Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.
- The recently released 16.3-inch MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage is on sale starting at $3,249 ($150 off) — a new low price — at Amazon and Best Buy. The redesigned laptop is Apple’s first with an OLED touchscreen, which allows for rich colors and deep blacks. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications. Read our review.
Apple MacBook Air (M5)
Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review.
- The 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is on sale starting at $1,849 ($150 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is a new low price. title_en: Nothing's AI device debuts December 8, and it looks like two vapes stuck together
title_fa: Nothing's AI device debuts December 8, and it looks like two vapes stuck together
excerpt_en: Thanks, Swedish House Mafia. I guess.
excerpt_fa: Thanks, Swedish House Mafia. I guess.
content_en:
Nothing's AI device debuts December 8, and it looks like two vapes stuck together
Thanks, Swedish House Mafia. I guess.
In classic Carl Pei fashion, Nothing has begun to trickle out details about its latest product. On Friday the company shared that it plans to officially debut the new "AI-native device" with "no new screen and an experience that couldn't have been built as an app," on December 8. And if that was all there was to report, we probably wouldn't be publishing this story, but a photo of gadget has lazily drifted across social media like a fat cloud of fruit-flavored nicotine, thanks an unlikely source. Drink it in:
@nothing pic.twitter.com/WgcWNI2dIc
— Sebastian Ingrosso (@Ingrosso) November 19, 2026
On Wednesday at 10:28PM ET, Sebastian Ingrosso of house music trio Swedish House Mafia posted a photo on social media with Nothing's official X account tagged. Between a pair of Nothing Headphone 1 Pro headphones and a MacBook Pro, we can see a device that clearly fits the description of a screenless gadget like the one described by Nothing. "Bro... y u leak?" one X user wrote in response to the Ingrosso's photo. Is this a coordinated marketing stunt by Nothing? (Yes, duh.) Decide for yourself.
The one thing I can't get over is the fact that it looks like two vapes put together. Judging from the teaser the company shared, it also has at least one camera, likely for some kind of visual intelligence feature. We'll reserve judgment until we see the new device in person, but right now it looks like a rare miss by Nothing's design team.
Joking aside, it will be interesting to see how Nothing positions this device; the track record for AI gadgets isn't exactly encouraging. Humane went out of business at the start of last year, and Rabbit has sort of plodded along ever since the debut of the R1.

title_en: You can reveal the full GTA 6 map in minutes using this simple plane trick
title_fa: You can reveal the full GTA 6 map in minutes using this simple plane trick
excerpt_en: Clear up that fog in no time at all, but be careful.
excerpt_fa: Clear up that fog in no time at all, but be careful.
content_en:
You can reveal the full GTA 6 map in minutes using this simple plane trick
Clear up that fog in no time at all, but be careful.
GTA 6 has a huge map, which is around twice as big as the one found with GTA 5. That's a whole lot of Florida-inspired strip malls and alligator-soaked swamps. However, new players start the game in a fairly remote region, based on the Florida Keys, and the vast majority of the map is unavailable for perusal.
Fog is obscuring every part of the map that you haven't explored yet. New regions get uncovered as you travel through them. You could do this the long way, by following the story. You could also do this the slightly-shorter way, by grabbing a car and just driving north until the wheels fall off. GTA 6 doesn't have a system in place that automatically ups the wanted level as you enter new areas, so that's good.
However, the quickest way to unlock the full map is found in the skies, and not the roads. Long-time players know the drill. Jason needs to get an airplane.
Finding a plane
Luckily, there's a plane just a few miles north of Jason's first house in Key Lento. Take a break from making home renovations and head to Southpoint Airfield, as seen in the map above. It's basically just north of the starting area.
Drive the western bridge that runs over the Shoeless Keys and then head west a little bit onto a runway. It's hard to miss. The area is marked as restricted, but it's mostly abandoned so there shouldn't be any armed onlookers.
Once at the airfield, look for a duster plane just waiting to be flown. Hop in and do your thing. Planes move incredibly fast and will quickly unlock all of those foggy areas. Just fly carefully and keep an eye on fuel.
You probably won't be able to get the whole map done on a single fly through, due to that fuel, but planes automatically regenerate at airfields as soon as one leaves. Fly back to Southpoint and start again, this time heading in another direction. You'll have the whole map uncovered in minutes.
Happy travels. The only real thing to worry about here is the Mile Zero Air Station at the bottom left of the map. Flying over that airspace will instantly generate a four-star wanted rating. This wanted level can bring police after you in helicopters, so airplanes aren't necessarily safe. Save this area for last and exit as soon as the fog lifts from the map. Mile Zero is home to some really fast aircraft, but it's likely not worth the trouble just yet.

Luckily, there's a plane just a few miles north of Jason's first house in Key Lento. Take a break from making home renovations and head to Southpoint Airfield, as seen in the map above. It's basically just north of the starting area.
Drive the western bridge that runs over the Shoeless Keys and then head west a little bit onto a runway. It's hard to miss. The area is marked as restricted, but it's mostly abandoned so there shouldn't be any armed onlookers.
Once at the airfield, look for a duster plane just waiting to be flown. Hop in and do your thing. Planes move incredibly fast and will quickly unlock all of those foggy areas. Just fly carefully and keep an eye on fuel.
You probably won't be able to get the whole map done on a single fly through, due to that fuel, but planes automatically regenerate at airfields as soon as one leaves. Fly back to Southpoint and start again, this time heading in another direction. You'll have the whole map uncovered in minutes.
Happy travels. The only real thing to worry about here is the Mile Zero Air Station at the bottom left of the map. Flying over that airspace will instantly generate a four-star wanted rating. This wanted level can bring police after you in helicopters, so airplanes aren't necessarily safe. Save this area for last and exit as soon as the fog lifts from the map. Mile Zero is home to some really fast aircraft, but it's likely not worth the trouble just yet.

excerpt_fa: Teenage Engineering announced what it describes as "a modern take on a classic CD player" with its new EP/BC-1 featuring a slab-like design that leaves the spinning disc exposed instead of hiding it under a lid or inside a slide-out tray. The company says the EP/BC-1 is the...
content_en:
Teenage Engineering announced what it describes as “a modern take on a classic CD player” with its new EP/BC–1 featuring a slab-like design that leaves the spinning disc exposed instead of hiding it under a lid or inside a slide-out tray. The company says the EP/BC–1 is the first entry in its new broadcast series of products and was designed to bring “physical audio formats into a modern context, evolved from a shared obligation within the company to preserve the formats they grew up with.”
Teenage Engineering’s first CD player puts the spinning disc on display
The EP/BC–1 can wirelessly stream audio to Bluetooth headphones or multiple devices using Auracast.
The EP/BC–1 can wirelessly stream audio to Bluetooth headphones or multiple devices using Auracast.
The EP/BC-1 is available now through Teenage Engineering’s online store for $299. The CD player joins the company’s existing EP–series of audio devices and has the same dimensions as its KO II synthesizer that launched in 2023 so it can be paired with, and connected to, other Teenage Engineering gear including the recently-announced EP-35 battery-powered amp.
Although it’s designed to play a nearly 45 year old medium, the EP/BC-1 features modern conveniences like variable speed playback, cue markers, a jog wheel for forward and reverse search, and built-in beat detection. There’s a very retro-looking series of digital displays showing track, index, time information, and audio levels, and around the edges you’ll find both digital and analog audio connections including a headphone jack and a USB 2.0 port.
If you want to go completely wireless the CD player has a rechargeable battery and supports both Bluetooth connections to headphones and Auracast streaming to multiple devices that support it. The EP/BC-1 is compatible with standard CDs as well as discs full of MP3 files, and when using the former it can rip tracks to 44.1 Hz/16-bit WAV files. If you want MP3s or other formats, you’ll need to convert them yourself.

title_en: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
title_fa: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
excerpt_en: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics's most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world's best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark...
excerpt_fa: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics's most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world's best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark...
content_en:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics’s most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world’s best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark yet another seismic achievement for AI in mathematics and add to the upheaval already unleashed by OpenAI’s previous, often inelegant forays into the field.
Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
An Anthropic mathmetician’s latest breakthrough is another sign of how quickly AI is transforming mathematics.
An Anthropic mathmetician’s latest breakthrough is another sign of how quickly AI is transforming mathematics.
Alpöge’s solution has yet to be verified independently. Anthropic has not commented or involved itself in Alpöge’s announcement. In a document on his website, Alpöge says he texted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about the solution “late Sunday night” and suggests he held off publication until after the company’s IPO on Thursday.
The Riemann hypothesis is one of seven Millennium Prize problems, which are widely considered some of the most formidable open challenges in mathematics. First proposed in 1859, the Riemann hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and how zeroes of a function are involved. It’s regarded as one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics.
A statement on Alpöge’s website says Claude was integral to developing the proof:
I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof1 of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.
The Verge reached out to Anthropic but didn’t immediately hear back. Anthropic said it was working on the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude in August, but noted at the time: “We don’t expect that the techniques Claude used will lead to proving the Riemann hypothesis.”
Alpöge’s solution, presented in Lean, has only been published on his website and has not yet been publicly accepted by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which administers the Millennium Prize and offers a $1 million bounty for each problem solved. Under the institute’s rules, a proposed solution must be published and withstand at least two years of scrutiny before it can be considered for the prize, during which time it must have “received general acceptance in the global mathematics community.”
In the quarter-century since the prize was established, only one problem has been officially solved: The Poincaré conjecture, a topological problem concerning three-dimensional spheres. In September, OpenAI claimed to have cracked another, the Navier-Stokes problem, which concerns the flow of fluids.
OpenAI said it pursued Navier-Stokes after hearing rumors that rival researchers were closing in on a solution. Alpöge had been working on the problem with New York University mathematics professor Tristan Buckmaster. Buckmaster claimed OpenAI produced a solution for Navier-Stokes using the route he and Alpöge were working on with OpenAI’s Codex and Claude.
OpenAI spent millions of dollars and deployed 10,000 agents in the attempt. The result is widely considered credible, though it has yet to receive formal recognition. But the achievement has been marred by allegations of questionable research practices, including claims it used unpublished work from mathematicians who had shared their research with its AI tools. OpenAI has strongly denied wrongdoing, but this has done little to quell the uproar.
Though most of the spotlight has been on OpenAI’s movement in math, Alpöge said in July that he solved the Jacobean conjecture using Claude. The deluge of findings has left mathematicians scrambling to digest the material and figure out where they belong in what is rapidly becoming a profoundly different mathematical landscape.

title_en: Boys Noize turns to the club (and an obscure Italian synth) for inspiration on 7LLVSION
title_fa: Boys Noize turns to the club (and an obscure Italian synth) for inspiration on 7LLVSION
excerpt_en: If you're wondering how Alex Ridha's (aka Boys Noize) collaboration with Nine Inch Nails influenced his new record 7LLVSION, the answer is simple: It didn't. That's not to say Ridha didn't learn anything from the virtuosic production team of Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross, but...
excerpt_fa: If you're wondering how Alex Ridha's (aka Boys Noize) collaboration with Nine Inch Nails influenced his new record 7LLVSION, the answer is simple: It didn't. That's not to say Ridha didn't learn anything from the virtuosic production team of Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross, but...
content_en:
If you’re wondering how Alex Ridha’s (aka Boys Noize) collaboration with Nine Inch Nails influenced his new record 7LLVSION, the answer is simple: It didn’t. That’s not to say Ridha didn’t learn anything from the virtuosic production team of Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross, but most of the songs on 7LLVSION had been knocking around for some time. And as Ridha is quick to point out, these are not rock songs built for live performance; they’re “battle tested” for clubs and DJ sets. “I was kind of back on the usual kind of thing,” he tells The Verge.
Boys Noize turns to the club (and an obscure Italian synth) for inspiration on 7LLVSION
‘I always look for the newest machines.’
“I do the same I kind of always do. I go make coffee, go in my room, put on the machines, and I’ll start messing around with sounds and build one sound to another and there comes a record,” he says. Like previous Boys Noize releases, a lot of 7LLVSION starts with sound design. “It’s kind of tech-driven, in a way,” he says, “because I always look for the newest machines.”
On 7LLVSION, Ridha frequently turned to an obscure Italian semimodular synth, the Grp A4. “It’s just so powerful, and it sounds so big,” he says. The routing options, dual filters (which he uses in parallel), and built-in sequencer kept leading him to new and inspiring places. Because of that, the A4 ended up on a number of tracks, including “Shut It Down,” “1+1+1,” and “Ycore.”.
“The exciting part is always to, you know, not repeat myself, even with the drum sounds, and try something new that I haven’t tried before,” Ridha says. For a few tracks, that meant getting away from the rigid, quantized grooves of techno and opting for a more dynamic, live feeling on tracks like “Shut It Down” and “1+1+1” especially. “Live drums are the new 808,” he says.
He looked to German bands of the ’70s and ’80s for inspiration, like Can, Amon Düül, and Deutsch Amerikanische Freundschaft. He also called out Conny Plank, who produced landmark records by Neu!, Kraftwerk, and Eurythmics. But in general he says, “My goal is to not sound like anything you can point to. You know, I don’t want to be a direct copy.” Instead, he was chasing the sound of “electronic punk.” That means aggressive basslines, driving drums, and stripped-down arrangements that avoid overstuffing the mix with too many instruments.
But it all comes back to the club at the end of the day. “Environment has always been the main thing in my music. I need to have a record that I want to play at the party,” he says, and that meant testing the songs off 7LLVSION extensively in his DJ sets and letting the audience tell him what works and what doesn’t. “The club is the most open and objective situation you can have,” he says. “They don’t know what I’m playing, so they hear something for the first time, and you can just look at someone’s face, or someone’s there in the room to get a cool reaction, and that usually makes me feel good about something or not.”
Boys Noize is currently touring the world on the festival circuit, and 7LLVSION is available now on most major streaming services.

title_en: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp for $3.68B
title_fa: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp for $3.68B
excerpt_en: Intuit acquired the company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so it looks like Bending Spoons is getting quite a bargain.
excerpt_fa: Intuit acquired the company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so it looks like Bending Spoons is getting quite a bargain.
content_en:
Bending Spoons has bought up another distressed internet company. This time, it’s the email marketing firm Mailchimp, bought for $3.68 billion from the tax-preparation giant Intuit.
Intuit acquired the company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so it’s taking quite a loss — and, perhaps, Bending Spoons is getting quite a bargain. At the time of the sale to Intuit, that acquisition caused headlines because Mailchimp employees reportedly received no equity, so no share of the sale proceeds, because the founders had allegedly promised them they didn’t need it as they would never sell.
Flash forward to now, with Intuit hit hard by the Death Star to SaaS trade — aka AI — with the company’s shares worth less than half what they were a year ago. The company told Reuters that the sale will let it sharpen its focus on AI tools for small businesses, and the new cash will be used to repurchase shares.
Bending Spoons describes the transaction as an all-cash deal, although that’s not quite true: As part of the same package, Intuit is buying $368 million in newly minted shares of Bending Spoons, so the net effect is a split of 90% cash to 10% stock.
Still, the transaction is a major pickup for Bending Spoons, which has become a kind of clearinghouse for late-stage web properties, with its game plan to hold them long term. In just the last year, the company has snapped up AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable, and Miro. Previous acquisitions include older stalwarts like Evernote, Meetup, and Vimeo. In each case, Bending Spoons integrated the products into centralized engineering and revenue systems, resulting in significant cost savings while often improving the available support and product resources.
“We want to place ourselves as an operator that takes beloved brands and makes them much better,” Bending Spoons co-founder and chief product officer, Matteo Danieli, told TechCrunch in July.
